title: Geo features and Objects
source: An operator interface receives the geo features and Objects Core holds, makes a geo feature, sends an Asset to it, edits and deletes geo features, and sees an edit refused.

steps.why: With the Asset descriptions, Core pushes every geo feature it holds: area G1.
and every Object: F1, an image Plugin IMG stored, attached to G1. The file stays in Core until the interface fetches it by object_id.
The operator marks a helipad. No geofeature_id, so this creates one.
Core picks the ID and returns it in the reply. A retry of the same message gets this same reply, so the ID is never lost.
Core sends the new geo feature to every operator interface.
The operator sends A1 to the helipad. The destination is a copy of G2's position; geofeature_id records where it came from. The Asset ignores it.
Core passes the Task on unchanged.
The operator widens G1. With geofeature_id, the message replaces the whole geo feature.
Every operator interface gets the new G1. F1 is still attached to it.
Core accepts. Task T1 is unchanged: it holds its own copy of the position, and G2 stays in it as a record. G2 is never reused in this run.
Every operator interface hears that G2 is gone.
The operator edits a geo feature Core does not hold.
Core refuses. Only Core makes IDs, so an edit never creates one.
